title: Universal Life Insurance Underwriting Retention Rule: Aggregate Face Limit per Insured
content:
## Rule

Ashgrove Universal Life Insurance coverage is aggregated per insured life, the insured being identified by insured name and date of birth together. A new policy is issued only if the face amount already in force on that insured plus the new face amount does not exceed **$25000000**, the aggregate face limit per insured.

The face amount already in force on the insured is the total face amount, at the date of evaluation, of every Ashgrove Universal Life Insurance policy on the same insured (same insured name and same date of birth) whose status is applied, in force, in the grace period, or overloan protected.

Two further provisions apply:

1. A policy issued by conversion of an Ashgrove term policy replaces the term face on the same date and never fails this limit for the face converted.
2. Face decreases always reduce the aggregate and are never refused on aggregate grounds.

## Points of judgement

- **Equality.** The test is "does not exceed": an aggregate of exactly $25000000 after the new policy is within the limit.
- **Which policies count.** A policy on the same insured that has lapsed, been surrendered, been returned under free look, been declined, or reached a death claim status does not enter the face already in force.
- **Same insured.** Two policies are on the same insured only when both the insured name and the insured date of birth match.

## Hypothetical cases

| Face in force on the insured | New face applied for | Total | Issued under this rule? |
|---|---|---|---|
| $18000000 | $7000000 | $25000000 | Yes, the total does not exceed the limit |
| $18000000 | $7500000 | $25500000 | No, the total exceeds the limit |
| $24000000, of which a $2000000 policy has lapsed | $3000000 | $25000000 counting only the $22000000 in force | Yes |

A face decrease of $1000000 on a policy of an insured whose in-force total stands above the limit is not refused on aggregate grounds.
